coverage: Denmark: five regions and 98 municipalities (GISCO 2024), with Christiansø kept outside the municipal and regional hierarchy. Greenland: five municipalities and the Northeast Greenland National Park (2020 geoBoundaries outline). Faroe Islands: all 29 municipalities from Umhvørvisstovan, May 2026. Greenland and the Faroe Islands open directly at their own location. The Danish regional merger takes effect in 2027 and is not applied early.
processing: All subdivisions use the shared regional renderer. Parent polygons are dissolved from one municipal topology; shared internal edges are stored once. Geometry is simplified together to about 33 m north-south after the source generalisation. Deeper levels load per parent. Land frontiers retain the existing France/Italy reference where present and are drawn once; reference border lines cross large lakes and sea channels independently of coastlines. Population retains the original reference date; no GDP values are inferred.

localAreas.coverage: Official DAGI parish. Parishes are ecclesiastical areas and may cross municipal boundaries. Navigation uses mapped land overlap, with the largest overlap as the primary municipality; all parish land parts are retained.
localAreas.processing: Official named areas retained. Danish parishes that cross municipal boundaries keep one identity and the same complete land geometry in each overlapping municipality; the largest overlap is used for primary navigation. Swedish local areas use the original GISCO municipality outline with detailed OpenStreetMap masks for Mälaren and Storsjön, restoring land removed by the coarse overview lake mask. Other areas are clipped to their existing municipality. Shared local topology simplified by 0.00003 degrees (about 3 m north–south), then clipped to the existing municipality land mask. Existing regional and municipal geometry is unchanged. Uncovered coastal slivers keep the municipality backdrop; no local administrative units or population estimates are invented.
